Forgotten Broncos running back could be a sleeper for key role in 2025
The Denver Broncos have an intriguing running back room that could become even more crowded this summer if the team signs veteran free agent J.K. Dobbins . RJ Harvey, the team's second-round draft pick in April, is the projected starter with Audric Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin the current top options to rotate in behind him (again, that could change if Dobbins signs). Behind them are Tyler Badie and Blake Watson. Most fans and pundits assume Badie and Watson are poised to have minimal roles in 2025, with one or both possibly even spending the season on the practice squad. But when coach Sean Payton was asked about the room's pass blocking last week, he specifically name-dropped just one of the team's backs. “They’re all… it’s not just one or two right now," Payton said. "Badie is very good in that area. So early on, we’re seeing all of them get the work. Then we’ll worry about [the detailed roles] as we get closer.” Badie (5-8, 197 pounds) has had an interesting career, and some fans have probably forgotten that he's still on the team. Broncos’ RB Depth Chart: Who Is Denver’s Starting Running Back After J.K. Dobbins Signing?
On June 10, the Denver Broncos signed free agent running back J.K. Dobbins, who played the 2024 season with division rival Los Angeles Chargers. The deal is for one year, $5.25 million. The running back room had become a pressing concern for head coach Sean Payton’s offense, with many expecting the team to draft one in the first round — a move they ultimately passed on. Now with Dobbins in the building, the question is: Who will be Denver’s starting running back? Who Will Lead the Denver Broncos’ Revamped Backfield in 2025? The Broncos’ run game in 2024 didn’t stand out, finishing just 16th in rushing yards per game with 112.2. It became clear the team needed reinforcements heading into 2025, especially now that Bo Nix appears to be the franchise quarterback and the offense has real breakout potential in its second year under Payton. Have the Denver Broncos found another undrafted gem? Following the 2025 NFL draft, Toledo wide receiver/returner Jerjuan Newton (5-11, 192 pounds) was among the players who landed in Denver as college free agents. Newton spent six years with the Rockets, including an impressive stretch in his final three seasons. The 23-year-old receiver totaled 177 receptions for 2,574 receiving yards and 29 touchdowns from 2022-2024. He earned first-team All-MAC honors after posting career highs in receptions (72), yards (1,048) and touchdowns (11) last fall.
